subject: Nimble monitors a node that was not requested

messages.author: bf6d77e39d193c5e
messages.subject: Nimble monitors a node that was not requested
parts:
Hello All, I have a distance sampling model that is running well. Nimble is monitoring 15 nodes that I specify with monitors=c(,,). However it is also monitoring a vector data (augmented) node 'd', the observed distances to each individual, which is making the output very large and slow.  I cannot figure out why nimble is monitoring this additional node and I would like it to stop.  Has anyone encountered this same issue before or know why nimble wants to monitor 'd' when it is not called for in the monitors argument?  None of my monitors even start with the letter d.
Thanks

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Nimble monitors a node that was not requested
parts: David, if you're able to send code for reproducing this behaviour (up through model building and building/configuring the MCMC), then hopefully I can take a look at what's going on.  Be default, nimble's MCMC should only monitor top-level parameters.  Is there a chance that one element of d is assigned a prior distribution?  In that case, the entirety of d would be monitored by default, as you described.

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Nimble monitors a node that was not requested
parts:
I'm not sure what workflow you're using to access the MCMC, but if you want to change this I'll suggest you don't use nimbleMCMC, but rather a workflow which includes configureMCMC and buildMCMC.

You can set the monitors to whatever you want, using the "monitors" argument to configureMCMC:

conf <- configureMCMC(..., monitors = ...)

Moreso, after creating the MCMC configuration object ("conf"), you can modify the monitors as you wish using methods such as:

conf$resetMonitors
conf$addMonitors
conf$setMonitors

and perhaps others.  See help(addMonitors) for details.

Cheers,
Daniel
